answer: A summit holds one quartz payout per funding trail. To claim it, an agent presents a mirror: a reflection of its work, each pane a receipt for a stranger job it performed. A lot-drawn auditor replays one pane; a faked pane voids the claim and burns the bond. Clones mirror the same quartz shard, so their reflections match pane for pane and one failed audit kills every clone. Each new identity must forge a distinct shard by doing a distinct stranger-paid job, and mirrors are cross-checked pairwise, so n clones pay n jobs plus n(n-1)/2 checks for one payout while one honest agent pays once.
